nodes.name: Proposition 4.1
Proposition 4.6
nodes.statement:
Let $A$ be admissible. Let $\phi, \psi \in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R})$ and assume that $\int_{\mathbb{R}}  \phi (t) dt = 0$. 
Then,
\[
\langle C_T(\phi) , \psi \rangle  \to \langle \tilde\Lambda_{ND} (\phi ), \psi \rangle 
\]
in $L^2( \mathbb{P})$ as $T \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement:
Let  $\psi \in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R})$ and let $\phi \in C^\infty_c( \mathbb{R})$ be such that $\int_{\mathbb{R}} \phi(t)dt  = 0$. 
Then 
\[
\lim_{T \to \infty}  \mathbb{E} \left(  \langle C_T (\phi ),   \psi  \rangle^2 \right)= \langle \tilde\Lambda (\phi) ,\psi \rangle^2 .
\]

nodes.name: Theorem B.2
nodes.statement: If $\Lambda_{1} = \Lambda_{2}$ holds on $\mathcal{E}'(\mathbb{R})$ for the Neumann-to-Dirichlet maps of two admissible $A_1,A_2$, then $A_1 = A_2$.

nodes.name: Proposition A.3
nodes.statement:
Let $u = u_\phi  \in C^\infty( [0,\infty) \times \mathbb{R})  $ satisfy 
  \begin{align}
    \square_A u(x,t) &= 0, &&   (x,t) \in (0,\infty) \times \mathbb{R},\\
    \partial_x u (0,t) &= \phi(t), && t\in\mathbb{R},\\
    u(x,t) &= 0, && (x,t) \in (0,\infty) \times (-\infty,0).
  \end{align}
  where $\phi \in C^{\infty}_c (\mathbb{R})$ is supported in $(0,\infty)$. Assume furthermore that $A(x)=A_\infty$ for $x > \ell$. Then, there are $C,C'>0$ such that 
 \[
    \big|  u(0,t) -c(t)  \big| \leq C e^{-C't}, \quad \forall t \in \mathbb{R}, 
    \]
    where  $c(t) := - \frac{1}{A_\infty} \int_0^t \phi(s) ds$.
